title: WDG Wars Go 0.9.19.2 - Clean Map. Same Loot.
notes:
RELEASE 0.9.19.2 - CLEAN MAP. SAME LOOT.

Fresh session, familiar cyberdeck. Less map clutter, better BLE memory, and an
updater that remembers doing its homework.

1. FRESH MAP. YOUR LOOT STAYS.

Before: Wi-Fi/BLE points from earlier sessions could reappear on the map.
Now: every launch starts with a clean Wi-Fi/BLE map. New receptions bring back both
new and known devices; repeats update the same session observation. Points stay
until you close the game, including after STOP and scheduled Wi-Fi/BLE switches. No
valid position means no map point.

A fresh map does not erase saved loot, logs, pending uploads, XP, levels,
achievements or settings. Your cyberdeck remembers the loot. The map is allowed to
forget.

2. BLE: NICE TRY, WE'VE MET

Before: some saved BLE addresses were missed after restarting, so an old
acquaintance could collect the full 10 XP welcome bonus again. Commas or unmatched
quotes in names could also confuse CSV entries, hide following records or scramble
names and positions in the history view. Some history reads left files open.
Now: supported current and older history entries retain their correct identities,
names, signal strength and positions. Following records stay separate, and readers
close their files. Old logs are not rewritten. Known BLE devices get 1 XP;
genuinely new BLE devices still get 10 XP. A known device joins the clean map only
after a new reception with a valid position.

Rebooting is not a witness protection programme.

3. ONE ADDRESS, TWO RECORDS

Before: Wi-Fi and BLE sharing the same address could overwrite or suppress each
other's WiGLE export entry.
Now: each protocol keeps its own record. A stronger signal updates only that
protocol's row; a weaker or equal signal leaves it intact. The other protocol's row
stays untouched.

The XP rules remain 15 XP for new Wi-Fi, 10 XP for new BLE and 1 XP for repeats.
Previously earned XP is neither recalculated nor taken away. Reading and
deduplicating history does not rewrite old logs or remove pending uploads.

4. PENDING LOGS: TAKE OUT THE PACKET TRASH

Before: exports without usable GPS could hang around after an upload attempt, with
no way to remove a selected pending file in the game.
Now: PLUGINS -> Pending Upload Logs lists individual Wi-Fi, ADS-B, MeshCore and
Meshtastic export files. Select one, press D, then Y to delete it or N / Esc to
cancel. The list is available without an upload API key.

After an upload attempt, inactive export files with no usable GPS records are
cleaned up automatically, without another question. Files containing any usable GPS
records stay. Active sessions, uploads in flight and files that change during the
operation are protected.

Deletion removes the selected export, not your progress: XP, levels, achievements,
contacts and known Wi-Fi/BLE identities stay. Known devices still earn repeat XP
after restarting. Discarding an old mesh export does not erase a newer reception or
invent an upload receipt.

Some packets never found themselves. They do not need a permanent room in your log
folder.

5. MESH: THE LAST PACKET GETS A SEAT

Before: a MeshCore/Meshtastic reception waiting to be processed just before OFF or
a protocol switch could disappear from the map immediately.
Now: waiting receptions are included in the OFF snapshot. Valid Node GPS or the
existing [RX GPS] fallback places a marker. A later credible fix can fill a missing
position for a node heard this session. Restarting keeps contacts and progress
while starting a fresh mesh map.

The existing OFF rule stays: mesh markers disappear between 5 and 10 minutes,
farther first. Repeated STOP does not extend deadlines; the other active protocol
keeps its markers. This fixes a reproduced software edge case; it does not
establish the cause of earlier radio reports.

6. MC / MT: THIS SESSION'S ROLL CALL

Before: the public main HUD had no MC/MT counters.
Now: MC: and MT: count unique nodes successfully registered this session: new or
known, with or without coordinates. Repeat packets do not add another node. Both
counters stay visible, so changing protocols keeps the session's earlier work in
view. OFF and protocol switches retain the counts; restarting resets them.

Saved contacts, session counters and visible map markers are different numbers. The
ready-radio icon and familiar WDG styling stay.

7. UP TO DATE HAS A MEMORY NOW

Before: a verified UP TO DATE result was lost after restarting the game.
Now: it survives reopening the update window and restarting, tied to the installed
version and code. R and the startup check still work. A newer release replaces the
status. Network failures remain errors; any retained earlier success is labelled
last verified. New-release notices still appear only once per release.

One less thing on the cyberdeck with the memory of a goldfish.

8. RELEASE NOTES, NOW FLUENT IN CYBERDECK

Before: Update Game could display raw Markdown and emoji its font could not draw.
Now: the shared English description is adapted automatically for WDG: readable
text, numbered yellow headings, dark title strips and spacing. The original font,
colours, window and nine visible rows stay. GitHub and Discord keep their emoji and
formatting.

9. FN+U: GIVE THOSE LABELS SOME ELBOW ROOM

Before: scrolling the terminal with Fn+U / Page Up could make the scroll indicator
overlap the line count.
Now: both labels have separate space in the header, including longer counts. Same
terminal, fewer typographical pile-ups.

10. THE FIRST RESTART STILL NEEDS A HUMAN

Before / Now: installation and restart rules are unchanged.

If the running updater is 0.9.17, 0.9.18 or 0.9.19, the first upgrade still needs
one manual relaunch. After installation, press Enter or Esc to close the game, then
start it again.

Updates performed by 0.9.19.1 or later restart automatically after successful
installation, including 0.9.19.1 -> 0.9.19.2. Preparation, cancellation and failure
do not restart the game.

11. CHECKED ON THE CYBERDECK

Software regressions cover history reopening, the 15 / 10 / 1 XP rules, saved-data
preservation, safe pending-log deletion and cleanup, mesh queues, counters,
persistent update status and note rendering. Recorded Meshtastic replays and real
driver-code contracts use controlled inputs. The original Pyxel renderer is also
checked on the uConsole.

Natural Wi-Fi/BLE reception with GPS and Meshtastic reception were observed in the
running 0.9.19.2 game on our uConsole. Fresh startup maps and retained points after
Wi-Fi/BLE switching and STOP were also checked. Software checks cover history
reopening, XP rules, saved-data preservation, mesh queues, counters, update status
and note rendering.

MeshCore reception remains unconfirmed by this device run. Physical RF reception
has not been verified for every profile or hardware setup. Recorded replays and
simulated transports do not prove new radio reception on other setups.

Original game by LOCOSP. Modified by KiloGramowy.

RELEASE 0.9.19.1 - ADS-B AND MESH OFF VISIBILITY
----------------------------------------------
1. AIRCRAFT AFTER ADS-B OFF
--------------------------
Before: 0.9.19 hid aircraft when ADS-B stopped and cleared them on STOP.
Changed: ADS-B OFF keeps the last visible aircraft on the map and small
radar. They start disappearing after 5 minutes, farther ones first;
the nearest disappear by 10 minutes. Repeated STOP does not reset this.

2. MESHCORE AND MESHTASTIC AFTER OFF
----------------------------------
Before: mesh markers remained until the game closed, even after OFF.
Changed: after switching a mesh protocol OFF, its markers disappear
between 5 and 10 minutes, farther ones first. The other active protocol
keeps its markers. Saved contacts remain available after map expiry.

3. KEEP AIRCRAFT WHILE RECEPTION CONTINUES
----------------------------------------
Before: a position older than 60 seconds disappeared even while other
messages from the same aircraft were still arriving.
Changed: with ADS-B ON, any new message keeps its last known position
visible. New coordinates move the marker. An aircraft disappears after
60 seconds without another message. No movement is invented.

4. RESUME RECEPTION AND RESTART
-----------------------------
Changed: turning reception back ON cancels the remaining OFF schedule.
Already expired markers do not return without a new observation.
Retained radio aircraft get 60 seconds to be heard again. The distance
order uses the receiver location at OFF; object coordinates do not move.
Restarting the game starts with an empty aircraft and mesh map.
Saved XP, badges, contacts, notes and logs remain unchanged.

5. EARLIER FIXES INCLUDED
------------------------
This is one cumulative installation, including the earlier progress,
BLE and contact-panel fixes. Saved mesh contacts do not reappear on the
map merely because the game restarted. The ADS-B and mesh OFF rules
above replace the corresponding historical 0.9.19 rules below.
Original game by LOCOSP. Modified by KiloGramowy.

6. UPDATE STATUS AND AUTOMATIC RESTART
------------------------------------
Before: a current check used a longer status message, and a completed
installation required closing and launching the game manually.
Changed: a verified current installation shows UP TO DATE. Updates
installed by the 0.9.19.1 updater restart the game automatically after
saving progress, stopping devices and completing the code replacement.
Cancelled, failed or merely prepared updates do not restart the game.
First upgrade from 0.9.17, 0.9.18 or 0.9.19: the running old updater
still needs one manual relaunch. After installation press ENTER or ESC
to close the game, then launch it again. Later updates restart it for you.

RELEASE 0.9.19 - MAP MICROFIX
---------------------------
Historical notes. ADS-B and mesh OFF policies are superseded by 0.9.19.1.

1. ADS-B MAP AND RADAR
---------------------
Before: old aircraft stayed visible after ADS-B stopped; other SBS
messages could keep an outdated position on screen.
Changed: both map views show positions received within 60 seconds from
an active ADS-B scan. A confirmed STOP clears the live aircraft cache.
A pending STOP is reported honestly. Saved XP and logs remain intact.

2. MESH MAP AFTER RESTART
------------------------
Before: startup and GPS backfill could put all saved mesh contacts on
the map, without receiving them in the current session.
Changed: MeshCore and Meshtastic map markers start empty after restart.
A contact appears after reception in this session. GPS backfill alone
does not restore historical markers. Contacts, notes, XP and logs stay
saved. Mesh markers received this session remain until the game closes.

3. CUMULATIVE UPDATE AND NOTES
-----------------------------
Before: the update window always displayed the entire published text.
Changed: 0.9.19 can select versioned sections for missing fixes in future
updates. One confirmation installs all missing code changes together.
Existing 0.9.17 and 0.9.18 readers show both sections during this first
transition. The 0.9.18 section below is for users upgrading from 0.9.17.

RELEASE 0.9.18 - PREVIOUS FIXES
-----------------------------
Catch-up for users upgrading from 0.9.17. Already on 0.9.18? These fixes
are already installed; the new changes are in the 0.9.19 section above.

WatchDogsGo 0.9.18
Original game by LOCOSP. Modified by KiloGramowy.

1. XP, LEVEL AND SAVED DATA
---------------------------
Before: an old v1 save could lose XP, badges, contacts and history.
Changed: preserve saved progress and counters; create a backup before
migration. Saved zero stays zero. Unsafe migration stops startup.
For a separate clone, run.sh accepts the old installation root as its
data argument. Already erased XP requires an intact save or backup.

2. BLE SCAN COMPLETION
----------------------
Before: Linux bridge results could end with a false scan timeout.
Changed: accept its final BLE scan done marker. Keep XIAO/projectZero
Summary support and save/STOP checks. Adapter warnings pause scanning;
late replies cannot restart a cancelled schedule.
Validation: bridge completion handling passes software tests. AC1200
hardware testing is pending; our own setup uses XIAO ESP32-C5.
The fix is expected to address this completion-marker mismatch when
the Linux adapters, drivers and bridge are already working.

3. MESHCORE CONTACT LIST
------------------------
Before: Ctrl+H hid an empty list; keys still reached the chat.
Changed: show CONTACTS (0), block chat input while the panel is open,
and close the empty panel with Esc without leaving chat. Keep the panel
visible after deleting the final contact.

4. MESHTASTIC CONTACT LIST
--------------------------
Before: Ctrl+H hid the panel when no contacts were saved.
Changed: show CONTACTS (0) and the empty-list message. Keep MeshCore and
Meshtastic contacts and panel states separate.

5. UPDATE NOTES
---------------
Before: change descriptions used one text color.
Changed: use numbered yellow titles on dark strips, underlines and blank
line; keep the factual description in white.
